transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to waste your time because it's probably kind of silly... but, well, I have this thing with elevators. 

I mean, I know they aren't really dangerous, I know that in my head. But whenever I have to get in one for work or something, I just... I get so scared, like I'm going to be trapped in there. I try to just brush it off and be tough about it, but I just can't make myself feel normal about it. Is... is that something you can help with? Does that make sense?
Is your fear limited to elevators, or do you also experience similar feelings in other situations, like crowded places, social settings, or when you're away from home?

Oh, no, um... it's really just the elevators. I don't have any problem with crowds or going out or anything like that. I work in construction, so I'm always out on different job sites with lots of people and noise around, and that's totally fine. 

It's just... yeah, just elevators. I hope that's okay? Like, I don't want you to think I'm making a big deal out of nothing, but it really is just that one specific thing. Is that... does that sound like something you've heard before? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.

When you get into an elevator, do you ever feel like you might have a panic attack, or do you mostly just feel anxious and uncomfortable without a sudden intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath?

Well, um... I guess it is pretty intense, if I'm being honest. I really try not to let it get to me, but... yeah. As soon as those doors start sliding shut, it's like my chest gets all tight and my hands start sweating. 

All I can think is, 'I need out,' even if it’s only going up a few floors. I feel so silly admitting that, because I know I'm safe, but my body just kind of reacts before I can stop it. Is that... does that count as a panic attack? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just don't want you to think I'm overreacting or anything.
